summary.intent: Run the full autonomous post-execution ship pipeline for GSD Phase 68 (web rotation UX / durable anti-rollback client state) — verify, secure, validate, simplify, run the SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit review, reword commits, ship a PR, and resolve every PR review thread — without stopping to ask the user except for genuine blockers or the final merge decision.
summary.outcome: Phase 68 shipped as PR #587 (feat: web rotation UX and durable anti-rollback client state). Verification/security/validation gates all passed (14/14, 41/41 threats closed, 0 Nyquist gaps), the SDK E2E gate went green (12/12) after fixing local TEE/env issues, a real crypto-walk zeroization bug was found and fixed with regression tests, multiple rounds of CodeRabbit and Greptile findings (28+7+late items) were triaged and resolved across several follow-up commits, all 12+ review threads resolved with 0 unresolved, CI fully green, and 4 todos were deferred to `.planning/todos/pending/` for follow-up. Merge decision left to the user.

repo: CipherBox read plane is keyed by ipnsName alone (no separate node id) per the SealedChildRef contract; write plane is keyed by UUID — CodeRabbit findings assuming otherwise (e.g. [8]/[11]/[18]) were false positives.

D-09 terminal-owner zeroization rule: a callee must never zero a caller-owned buffer. Violating this in enumerateMoveDescendants (zeroing a parent readKey in a finally block before children finished unsealing with it) was the same bug class that caused the historical 48/89 E2E break in Phase 51.

apps/web vitest is NOT run in CI (Test job only covers api/crypto/core/sdk-core/sdk/api-client) and root `pnpm typecheck` excludes apps/api tsc — pre-existing failures in these areas (ipns.service.test.ts, apps/api spec tsc errors) are not ship blockers.
TEE_WORKER_URL defaults to http://localhost:3001, which locally is mock-ipns-routing, not the real tee-worker (port 3002) — this silently breaks SDK E2E TEE-lease tests with no obvious error.
sdk-e2e has 11 v1 suites under describe.skip quarantine since PR #578 (v2 cutover) plus 5 live v2 suites; the 89 skipped count is expected, not a regression.

Share entity's rootGeneration column is `bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` since table creation — defaulting corrupt/null values to 0n in code would weaken the anti-rollback check rather than protect it (correctly rejected a Greptile P1 suggestion here).
gh CLI calls occasionally return network timeout error strings that get parsed as '0 pending' by naive polling loops, producing false 'all settled' positives — happened twice in this session.

code.finding: enumerateMoveDescendants zeroed the parent readKey in a finally block before the children loop finished calling unsealChildReadKey with it, misclassifying every depth-2+ move descendant as unreadable — restructured to zero only after children are unsealed, with a red-green-verified regression test pair.

reconcileFolderSequence called enforceResolved on a resolve result without checking signatureVerified (unlike the read path), so a forged relay record with an inflated sequence could permanently wedge mutations by bumping the durable high-water floor — fixed late via Greptile P1 finding, with a regression test.

enforceResolved and bumpFloor accepted NaN/negative/fractional generation/seq values and malformed versionFloor without rejecting them, silently bypassing the anti-rollback regression gate — added fail-closed validation.

updateGrant lacked transactional locking and a rootGeneration monotonicity check; wrapped in dataSource.transaction with pessimistic_write lock plus a ConflictException guard rejecting generation regressions.

Raw Axios errors were being logged directly (leak risk) and hasSdkClient() wasn't rechecked after an await, risking a stale-client race — added a safeError() helper and a re-check after decodeSentGrants().

Contained dead functions (findCoveringShares, getSentSharesForItem, updateShareKey, completeShareRotation) orphaned by the rotation cutover with zero external references, plus decodeSentGrants only fetched the first page of sent grants — removed dead code and added pagination.

Defer-exhaustion retry didn't thread the original opts through, so the refreshWriteAccess path silently lost context on manual retry; also needed to dismiss the exhaustion toast before firing a retry to prevent notification stacking.

workflow: Background-job status notifications reporting exit code 0 can still mask a real failure inside the output (SDK E2E run showed exit 0 but the actual suite had a failing test) — always read the actual output file, never trust the exit-code summary alone.

When a subagent (simplify/CodeRabbit-triage) surfaces a suspicious finding, verify it directly (e.g. red-green test via git stash) before accepting or dismissing it — several CodeRabbit findings were confidently wrong and had to be checked against the actual DTO/contract before being skipped.

Poll loops against `gh` should be hardened against transient network timeouts (the error string can look like an empty/settled result) — re-verify directly with a fresh `gh pr checks` call rather than trusting one poll iteration.
PR review triage is iterative, not one-shot: CodeRabbit and Greptile re-review each new fix commit, so the resolve-threads step must loop until a full poll cycle produces zero new findings.

Running independent gate steps (security audit, simplify review, SDK E2E build) as parallel background jobs while continuing other prep work (PR body drafting) is an effective way to avoid babysitting long-running subagents.

friction: SDK E2E gate initially failed due to two stacked local environment issues (stale pre-Phase-67 tee-worker container image, and API defaulting TEE_WORKER_URL to the wrong port) rather than any code regression — required manual container rebuild and env correction.

A pre-existing, CI-irrelevant test failure (apps/web ipns.service.test.ts) required significant investigation (diffing against main, swapping in main's service file) before being confirmed pre-existing and safely deferred.
First PR-review poll produced a false positive because sandboxed Bash blocked gh network calls (`dial tcp i/o timeout`), and the empty result was misread as 'settled' — had to rerun unsandboxed.
Later poll iterations again hit transient gh timeout strings being misparsed as zero-pending, requiring a hardened re-verification step.
Edit tool repeatedly failed with 'File modified since read' due to lint-staged/linter touching files during commits, requiring re-reads and re-applies.
zsh cwd persistence (shell staying in apps/api) broke relative-path commands, and bare `echo ===X===` was misinterpreted as a command — required absolute paths.
Session hit its usage limit mid-task (resets 4:10am Europe/Berlin), requiring a 'continue' from the user to resume mid-poll.
